narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and your property ownership situation. Your checking account status was the single biggest reason for the denial. Having a negative balance pushes the prediction quite strongly toward bad credit risk, especially since only 12.6% of approved applicants are in this situation while the majority maintain positive or zero balances.

The shorter 12-month duration you requested actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval. Most approved loans average 19 months, so your more modest timeframe was viewed positively by the model.

Unfortunately, having no recorded property worked against you and added further weight toward the bad credit prediction. Only 7.8% of approved applicants lack any property, whereas most own a car, real estate, or insurance-linked assets.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude your application carried too much risk. To improve your chances next time, focus on clearing your checking account into positive territory and, if possible, acquiring a tangible asset that can be documented. Once those areas improve, reapply. Many people in similar situations successfully obtain loans after making these adjustments. (248 words)
